commit_message:
[compiler] Template methods in SimplifiedLowering pt. 4

This is a CL in a string of CLs that template SimplifiedLowering.
It is done with the purpose of decoupling the implementation in the
three phases that SimplifiedLowering has (Propagate, Retype, Lower).

Template lower(), retype() and propagate(). Remove phase_ since it is
not needed anymore.

Template methods that used the old version of lower() and similar:
 * EnqueueInput
 * SetOutput
 * ProcessInput
 * VisitLeaf
 * VisitSelect
 * VisitPhi
 * VisitStateValues
 * VisitFrameState
 * VisitObjectState

findings.title: Missing control-input guard in InsertUnreachableIfNecessary<LOWER> crashes on pure nodes
findings.message: In `InsertUnreachableIfNecessary<LOWER>`, the ternary expression used to select a control node unconditionally calls `NodeProperties::GetControlInput(node, 0)` whenever `ControlOutputCount() == 0`. This assumes that any node without control outputs must have at least one control input. However, pure nodes (operator property `kPure`, e.g. `kSameValue`) have zero control inputs AND zero control outputs. When such a node produces a value of type `None` (e.g. through a type narrowing that makes the result impossible), the function is entered and `GetControlInput(node, 0)` triggers a CHECK failure in node-properties.h because `0 < node->op()->ControlInputCount()` is false (ControlInputCount is 0).
findings.suggestion: Before accessing the control input, check whether the node actually has control inputs. If the node has neither control inputs nor control outputs (i.e. it is a pure node), return early without inserting an Unreachable node, since there is no control edge to attach it to.

ground_truth.root_cause: The ternary guard `(node->op()->ControlOutputCount() == 0) ? GetControlInput(node, 0) : FindSuccessfulControlProjection(node)` only distinguishes between nodes with and without control outputs. It fails to handle the third case: pure nodes that have neither control inputs nor control outputs. This oversight was introduced when the function was refactored into a `<LOWER>` template specialization in 2020.
